hypothesis: In some types of non-Alzheimer's, non-aged human brain cells, for example astrocytes, APOE4 causes reduced endosome pH compared with APOE3.
A: APOE genotype or apoE isoform (APOE4 vs APOE3)
scope: IN: endosomal or endolysosomal luminal pH/acidity, and lysosomal pH as a neighbouring compartment (a contrary or related result); acidity probes of those compartments (ratiometric dextran/transferrin pH probes, LysoTracker, LysoSensor, pHrodo when read as acidity); regulators on the path to endosomal pH (NHE6/NHE9 expression or function, V-ATPase, the HDAC-CREB-NHE6 axis) measured or manipulated in an APOE4 context. OUT: mitochondrial/mitophagy pH, mTOR or other signalling readouts, whole-proteome changes, cell viability, amyloid or cargo uptake not read as compartment acidity.

row.Finding description: Human isogenic APOE33 and APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia showed no significant difference in baseline late-endosomal/lysosomal pH, reported as approximately 5.15, with three wells per group.
row.Finding quote: While baseline LE/Ly pH did not differ between APOE33 and APOE44 iMG (∼5.15), APOE33 iMG exhibited further acidification upon challenge (∼5.05), whereas APOE44 iMG failed to do so (Figure 3G).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in baseline late-endosomal/lysosomal pH in human iPSC-derived microglia)
row.Experimental system: Human isogenic APOE33 and APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia from the male KOLF background; Jackson Laboratory lines JIPSC001000 and JIPSC001150. Untreated baseline late-endosomal/lysosomal pH measured ratiometrically with dextran polymers labeled with pH-sensitive ApHID and pH-independent Alexa 647; three wells per group, nine imaging frames per well. Donor age and AD status were not specified for this isogenic pair.
row.Data location: Fig 3G, untreated APOE33 vs untreated APOE44

proposed.why: Isogenic APOE33 vs APOE44 with ratiometric dextran late-endosomal/lysosomal (endolysosomal) pH: A varied and B measured, same measurement as reference P3.F1 (1/2).

row.Finding description: After organoid-debris challenge, human isogenic APOE33 microglia acidified from about pH 5.15 to 5.05 (*** vs untreated APOE33 in Fig 3G), whereas APOE44 microglia did not acidify significantly (ns vs untreated APOE44); debris-treated APOE44 late-endosomal/lysosomal pH was about 0.08 units higher than debris-treated APOE33 (about 5.13 vs 5.05, read from Fig 3G), with three wells per group.
row.Finding quote: While baseline LE/Ly pH did not differ between APOE33 and APOE44 iMG (∼5.15), APOE33 iMG exhibited further acidification upon challenge (∼5.05), whereas APOE44 iMG failed to do so (Figure 3G).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (impaired challenge-induced late-endosomal/lysosomal acidification in human iPSC-derived microglia)
row.Experimental system: Human isogenic APOE33 and APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia from the male KOLF background; Jackson Laboratory lines JIPSC001000 and JIPSC001150. Organoid-debris challenge followed by ratiometric late-endosomal/lysosomal pH imaging using dextran-conjugated ApHID and Alexa 647; three wells per group, nine frames per well. Challenge duration and donor age/AD status were not specified in the supplied text.
row.Data location: Fig 3G, APOE33+debris vs APOE44+debris (also each vs its untreated genotype)

proposed.why: Same ratiometric dextran endolysosomal pH readout across genotypes after debris challenge as P2.F1 and reference P3.F1 (1/2).

row.Finding description: In the female UCI5 isogenic pair, organoid-debris challenge lowered APOE33 microglial late-endosomal/lysosomal pH (about 5.30 to 5.24, * vs untreated in Fig 7M) but raised APOE44 pH (about 5.29 to 5.40, *** vs untreated); debris-treated APOE44 pH was about 0.17 units higher than debris-treated APOE33 (about 5.40 vs 5.24, read from Fig 7M), with three wells per group.
row.Finding quote: Upon challenge with organoid debris, UCI5 APOE44 iMG lysosomes failed to mount an adaptive acidification response and instead shifted toward alkalinization (Figure 7M).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (impaired adaptive endolysosomal acidification, with challenge-induced alkalinization reported in APOE4 microglia)
row.Experimental system: Human iPSC-derived microglia from the additional female UCI5 APOE33/APOE44 isogenic pair, assayed untreated and after organoid-debris challenge. Late-endosomal/lysosomal acidity measured ratiometrically with dextran polymers labeled with ApHID and Alexa 647; three wells per group, 25 frames per well. Donor age, AD status, and challenge duration were not specified in the supplied text.
row.Data location: Fig 7M, UCI5 (33)+debris vs UCI5 (44)+debris (also each vs its untreated genotype)

proposed.why: Same ratiometric dextran endolysosomal pH readout in a second isogenic pair as P2.F1 and reference P3.F1 (1/2).

row.Finding description: Proteomics comparing human isogenic APOE44 with APOE33 microglia found significant downregulation of 53 of 84 identified lysosomal hydrolases and V-ATPases, without separately reporting the V-ATPase subset.
row.Finding quote: Of the 84 identified lysosomal hydrolases and V-ATPases, 53 were significantly downregulated in APOE44 iMG, supporting lysosomal impairment (Figure S3D).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (lower abundance of a combined lysosomal hydrolase/V-ATPase protein set)
row.Experimental system: Proteomic analysis of human isogenic APOE33 and APOE44 iPSC-derived microglia from the male KOLF background; Jackson Laboratory lines JIPSC001000 and JIPSC001150. Identified lysosomal proteins were assessed for differential abundance. This measures a protein set containing acidification regulators rather than luminal pH itself.
row.Data location: Supplementary Fig S3D; numerical counts reported in main Results

proposed.why: Was 3/3. Abundance of a lysosomal hydrolase/V-ATPase protein set is a regulator-level surrogate for endosomal pH that falls with lysosomal biogenesis changes independent of pH, matching the V-ATPase/NHE expression references P5.F2, P6.F3, P6.F7 (3/4).

row.Finding description: APOE4 astrocytes showed significantly higher lysosomal LysoTracker mean intensity than isogenic APOE3 astrocytes (about 41 vs 55 a.u. read from Fig 3G, ~35% higher), consistent with increased acidic-compartment staining but without a measured luminal pH difference.
row.Finding quote: We also observed that ApoE4 increased the intensity of LysoTracker, which is positively associated with lysosomal ac- tivity (Figure 3G
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosomal LysoTracker intensity in human astrocytes)
row.Experimental system: Human AG10788 AD-donor iPSC-derived APOE4 astrocytes and CRISPR-corrected isogenic APOE3 astrocytes; donor female, age 87; serum withdrawn at least 4 days; LysoTracker Red DND-99 staining at 250 nM for 30 minutes, fixation, confocal imaging, and mean signal-intensity quantification; no ratiometric pH calibration.

proposed.why: Was 3/3. Uncalibrated LysoTracker intensity on the lysosomal pool, the same readout as references P4.F1, P9.F2, P10.F1 (3/5).

row.Finding description: Four-day methyl-β-cyclodextrin treatment lowered elevated LysoTracker intensity in APOE4 astrocytes; cholesterol is a downstream intervention target and LysoTracker intensity is an indirect acidity readout.
row.Finding quote: We further observed restoration of lysosomal activity, as indicated by the mitigated intensity of LysoTracker after lysosomal cholesterol depletion (Figures 4D and 4F).
row.Finding summary: (cholesterol depletion in APOE4 astrocytes) -> (lower lysosomal LysoTracker intensity)
row.Experimental system: Human AG10788 AD-donor iPSC-derived APOE4 astrocytes, female donor age 87; methyl-β-cyclodextrin versus untreated APOE4 cells for 4 days; confocal quantification of lysosomal LysoTracker intensity; no calibrated luminal pH measurement.
row.Data location: Fig 4F, APOE4 plus methyl-β-cyclodextrin versus untreated APOE4

proposed.why: Was 5/3. Cyclodextrin does not act on APOE (genotype held at APOE4) and the readout is uncalibrated LysoTracker, matching the class 5 non-APOE manipulations with lysosomal readouts P9.F3, P9.F4 and P6.F9 (5/5).
proposed.reason_for_description: Class 5 because the perturbation is methyl-beta-cyclodextrin cholesterol depletion with APOE genotype held at APOE4, a lipid manipulation that does not act on A or a surrogate of A.

row.Finding description: FITC–dextran/Texas Red–dextran imaging of isogenic human iPSC-derived cortical neurons, using three plates with two wells per plate per genotype, showed no significant difference in endolysosomal pH between APOE4 and APOE3 or the other APOE genotypes.
row.Finding quote: Our results show that endolysosomal pH is not changed in any of the APOE isoform-expressing cortical neurons (Fig. 3C,D).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in endolysosomal pH in human iPSC-derived cortical neurons)
row.Experimental system: Human cortical neurons differentiated from EBiSC isogenic iPSC lines APOE ε3/ε3 (BIONi010-C-2), APOE ε4/ε4 (BIONi010-C-4), APOE ε2/ε2 (BIONi010-C-6), and APOE-null (BIONi010-C-3); neuronal age at assay not specified. Neurons were loaded with 500 µg/ml pH-sensitive FITC–dextran and 250 µg/ml pH-insensitive Texas Red–dextran for 24 h, followed by a 24 h chase in fresh medium. Operetta imaging measured FITC/Texas Red fluorescence ratios within Texas Red-positive cell-body vesicles, averaged per well; three plates with two wells per plate were imaged per genotype.
